An annuity or pension

An annuity or pension, mostly for life, at the Exchequer or out of a county's issues: how the king retained servants, knights and followers. Read a year.

Further reading: J. M. W. Bean, From Lord to Patron: Lordship in Late Medieval England (Manchester, 1989); Given-Wilson (1986).

How this was made
  1. Searched. Every canonical entry of the Patent, Close, Fine, Charter and Liberate Rolls (a second reading of the same act is counted once, as the corpus does). Here: the entries whose opening words this kind's rule matches, the first rule to speak among the kinds tried in order (what the king took, then debts between subjects, then what he paid). 4,086 of them name money.
  2. The sum. For this kind: the first sum that is not the value or rent of land. Then the words just before and after that sum are asked what it is (its role): a sum whose role is no price (the value or rent of land, a tax, a sum sued for, a penalty, money moved, a page reference) is set aside, and the entry's other sums are asked in turn. 3,967 are priced.
  3. The unit. Once, a day or a year, from the words after the sum ("a day", "yearly", "for life ... at the Exchequer"). This page shows the 3,113 sums paid a year; the others are in the table of roles.
  4. Counted. Each entry once. A grant enrolled on two rolls, or recited later, is here twice; the ward and confirmation series count such copies once, and this kind is not yet so counted.
  5. Real terms. "At 1300 prices" divides by Gregory Clark's price index; "years of pay" by a worker's yearly earnings in his series (MeasuringWorth).
  6. Read by hand. The roles were checked by reading 8 to 10 entries of each, the latest reading after the last change: a price paid to the king 9 of 10, a payment by the king 7 of 8, a farm or render 7 of 8, a debt to the king 7 of 8, a value or rent 7 of 8; a debt between subjects, a loan, a fine for an offence, a sum sued for, a tax, a penalty, money moved and not money 8 of 8 each. This kind has not been read entry by entry.

The rule for the kind, as written (a regular expression, matched in the first 420 characters):

\bfor\s+li(?:fe|ves)\b[^;]{0,160}?\bof\s+\d[\d,]*\s*(?:marks?|l\.|li\.|s\.|d\.)\s+(?:yearly|a\s+year)|\d[\d,]*\s*(?:marks?|l\.|li\.|s\.|d\.)\s+(?:yearly|a\s+year)\s+(?:at|from|out\s+of)\s+the\s+(?:exchequer|issues|customs|farm|receipt|hanaper|wardrobe)|\bannuity\b

Every sum

Goods prices hardly moved, so "at 1300 prices" looks like marks; pay rose about x2.5 by 1440, so years of pay sit lower after 1350.

By the rolls

The Patent and Charter Rolls hold grants and licences under the great seal; the Close and Liberate Rolls, writs and orders (the Liberate Rolls were split from the Close Rolls for writs of payment); the Fine Rolls, fines and commitments. A trend can be a change of roll or of calendar: read it beside this table.

The other money: a value or a rent
